evidence: M-O s.v. sensor: sensorium, i n. “Boethius and NL writers, of sensory organs in animals”
terms.comment: Lewis & Short has the word once, in Boethius, for the seat or organ of sensation; Morgan–Owens gives it for the device. The e is long before ns, as in sēnsus.

evidence: M-O s.v. sensor: instrumentum sensorium (Egger S.L. 14)

phrases.latin: Manum epitoniō subjice; sēnsōrium aquam ēmittet.
phrases.english: Put your hand under the tap; the sensor will let the water out.

phrases.latin: Jānua nōbīs appropinquantibus aperītur; sēnsōrium enim nōs sentit.
phrases.english: The door opens as we come near; the sensor feels us coming.

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. sensor.
